Hi Sarah 	6 thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by details and numbers you can share with procurement/ops.

1) Isolation boundaries (Dedicated)- In our Dedicated offering customers get reserved GPU pools and isolated serving pods. For most models we allocate dedicated instances (no multi-tenant vGPU sharing) per customer group, so noisy-neighbor interference at the GPU scheduling / kernel level is eliminated. Networking and process isolation is enforced at the pod/VM boundary. In short: Dedicated = single-tenant execution for the allocated capacity.

2) SLOs and predictable throughput- We offer SLA-backed latency tiers for Dedicated customers; exact contractual SLOs are defined by committed capacity and model profile. Operationally we provide per-route throughput guarantees by sizing a reserved pool (example below). We also provide burst capacity and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if capacity is exceeded (configurable).

Example sizing baseline (approximate, depends on model):
- For an Llama-2-13B style model: a single A100-equivalent GPU can sustain roughly 80-120 concurrent short-context generation streams at 10-20 tokens per request before p95 latency approaches the 200ms target (numbers depend on sequence lengths and tokenizer).
- For your peak 1,000 rps with p95 < 200ms, we'd typically recommend a reserved pool of ~10-14 GPUs plus autoscaling headroom and a small warm standby for burst events. We'll refine this in a sizing session with your exact prompt distribution and sequence lengths.

3) Noisy-neighbor mitigation and observability- Dedicated eliminates intra-tenant GPU contention. We additionally provide per-tenant token-level latency traces, KV-cache hit metrics, and per-route tail-latency dashboards in the Redwood Console so your SREs can monitor and alert.

4) Private / VPC differences- Private (VPC/on-prem) provides the same serving runtime but with customer-managed networking, KMS integrations, and optionally air-gapped deployments 	6 useful if you have regulatory customers requiring dedicated VPC or on-prem. The isolation there is strict and under your network boundary.

5) Trial / PoC- We can run a time-boxed eval against a mirrored traffic profile. Typical PoC structure: 1 week of scaled traffic replay with pre-agreed SLO targets and monitoring hooks; we provide instrumentation and a joint runbook.

Attachments included: redwood-dedicated-architecture.pdf (architecture diagram), SOC2-summary.pdf (control summary), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposed milestones).

Next steps
- Do a 60-min capacity sizing session where we: review model, traffic shapes, and pick a committed pool size.
- Agree on PoC scope and timeline (if you want to validate before committing).

Available slots next Tue/Wed (PST). Priyom: can you coordinate with procurement and send a calendar invite?

Cheers,
